肺.meaning: At a night <part>market</part>, one stall sells jars of fresh mountain air. The <part>moon</part> buys a dozen, takes a huge breath and swells to twice its size, glowing pink. Two big air bags puff in and out inside it: it has <kanji>lungs</kanji>.
肺.on: Its sigh blows a <sound>hi</sound>ve off the next stall, and the bees chase it home.

鋳.meaning: For her hundredth birthday, a toast to her <part>longevity</part>, Grandma gets a statue. Glowing <part>gold</part> is poured into a mould of her, hissing and spitting. When the mould cracks open, a shiny little Grandma gleams back. That's <kanji>casting</kanji>.
鋳.on: The sculptor seals one crack in the mould with a blob of <sound>chew</sound>ing gum.
鋳.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k, it's still hot!' squeals the real Grandma, poking its golden nose.

詐.meaning: A salesman gives a grand <part>speech</part> at the fair: his <part>coat rack</part> is a magic tree that grows a fresh coat every night. People pay a fortune. Next morning every rack is bare, apart from one sock he hung there himself. The whole thing was a <kanji>lie</kanji>.
詐.on: He runs off with the money hidden in a <sound>sa</sound>rdine tin.
詐.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' he shrieks, sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and slips in a puddle of <sound>wa</sound>sabi as the crowd chases him.

欺.meaning: A librarian lets out a huge <part>yawn</part> and pretends to doze. A thief tiptoes up to the <part>bookshelf</part> for the rare book, and the whole shelf swings round, spinning him into a locked cupboard. The sleepy librarian was pure <kanji>deceit</kanji>.
欺.on: The trick shelf turns on a giant hidden <sound>gear</sound>.
欺.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' yells the thief, stuck in the dark with a rug from a ba<sound>za</sound>ar and a stuffed <sound>moo</sound>se head.

硫.meaning: Near a hot spring, a <part>squid</part> wraps its arms round a bright yellow <part>stone</part> and won't let go. Every diver who swims by holds their nose: the rock smells of rotten eggs. The squid adores it. Its treasure is a lump of <kanji>sulphur</kanji>.
硫.on: It brings the stone to every family <sound>reu</sound>nion, and everyone groans.

愉.meaning: A retired astronaut builds a little <part>spaceship</part> in his garden for the neighbourhood cats. They curl up in it in the sun, purring so loud he can feel each <part>heartbeat</part> through the hull. He watches with his tea, grinning: pure <kanji>pleasure</kanji>.
愉.on: He rolls the cats a <sound>yu</sound>zu to bat around the cockpit.
愉.kun: He munches a <sound>ta</sound>co and sighs, '<sound>No</sound>t a bad life.'
